mainTopic: Worn coins: the measure of אונאה, time limits for returning them, and how worn a coin can be and still be used
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about worn coins and then explains it with a ברייתא. The משנה gives רבי שמעון's measure of one-sixth and sets time limits for returning a worn coin: in cities, until you could show it to a money changer, and in villages, until ערב שבת. It adds that a coin the giver recognizes must be taken back even after a year, and that a slightly worn coin is fine for מעשר שני. The גמרא settles an apparent contradiction with a ברייתא: רב פפא says the two simply count in opposite directions. רבא and אביי explain why the תנאים argue about coins but not about garments. The full ברייתא then lists three measures of אונאה and says how worn a coin can get and still be used. אביי and רבא show that the דינר, like the סלע, may wear down to half its value. The ברייתא's wording supports רבי אמי that a דינר made from a worn שקל may be kept. Finally, רב הונא and רבי אמי argue over a rule from a משנה in כלים, and the גמרא begins an objection that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's measure: one-sixth of the coin
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes רבי שמעון's opinion: a סלע worn down by eight פונדיונות, which is two פונדיונות per דינר, is still within the accepted range.
steps.simpleTranslation: Eight pundeyon, which is two pundeyon for each dinar.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing the last opinion in a list about how worn a coin can be before it counts as cheating. This line is רבי שמעון's amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is worth 4 דינרים, and each דינר is worth 12 פונדיונות, so a סלע equals 48 פונדיונות. Eight פונדיונות out of 48, or two out of every 12, is exactly one-sixth. That is the familiar one-sixth measure used for אונאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin; 12 of them make a דינר
A silver coin; 4 of them make a סלע

phrases.english: Eight pundeyon, two pundeyon per dinar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of opinions from the earlier part of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the measure for a worn סלע is eight פונדיונות, which is one-sixth of its value.

steps.title: Time limit for returning a worn coin
steps.stepSummary: In cities, a worn coin can be returned only within the time it takes to show it to a money changer. In villages, it can be returned until the next ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until when may a person return the worn coin? In big cities, until he has had time to show it to a money changer. In villages, until the eve of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now asks how long a person has to give back a worn coin he received. The answer depends on where he lives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deadline is set by how long it would reasonably take to find out the coin is worn. A city has money changers, so he can check quickly. In a village there is no expert, so he has until ערב שבת, when people go shopping and would notice the problem. If he waits past that point, it looks like he has accepted the coin.

keyTerms.meaning: To return (the coin)
Large walled cities
Money changer; an expert in coins
Villages
The days before שבת, when people shop

phrases.english: Until when is it permitted to return it?
In the cities: until enough time for him to show it to a money changer,
In the villages: until Shabbat eves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting how worn a coin must be, the משנה sets a deadline for returning it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A worn coin may be returned in cities within the time needed to show it to a money changer, and in villages until ערב שבת.

steps.title: A recognized coin must be taken back even after a year
steps.stepSummary: If the person who gave the coin recognizes it as his, he must take it back even after twelve months, and the other side has only a complaint.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he recognizes the coin, he must take it back from him even after twelve months, and he has nothing against him except a complaint.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception to the time limits. If the giver recognizes the coin as the one he gave, the deadlines do not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the deadline protects the giver, because after that time no one can be sure the coin is really his. Once he recognizes it, there is no doubt, so he must take it back even a full year later. The last phrase limits the claim to a תרעומת, a complaint with no legal force. The גמרא will explain who complains against whom.

keyTerms.meaning: Recognizes it (the coin)
He must accept it back
Twelve months
A complaint or grievance, with no legal claim behind it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'he has only a complaint' as saying the recognized coin need not be returned. The משנה just said he must take it back. The complaint is a separate point, and the גמרא will explain it later.

phrases.english: If he recognized it,
even after twelve months
he must accept it back from him,
and he has only a grievance against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the time limits of the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coin the giver recognizes must be taken back even after twelve months; beyond that, there is only a complaint.

steps.title: A slightly worn coin may be used for מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: A slightly worn coin may be used to redeem מעשר שני without worry, because only a stingy person would refuse it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may give the coin for מעשר שני and need not worry, because someone who refuses it is just being stingy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by saying a slightly worn coin is still a proper coin, good enough even for redeeming מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מעשר שני you need a real coin of full value, so you might think a slightly worn one is a problem. The משנה says it is fine, because the coin is fully accepted. A person who would turn it down is not being careful about the law; he just has a נפש רעה, a stingy nature.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe; produce that can be redeemed with money, which is then spent in ירושלים
He need not be concerned
A stingy or miserly nature

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rules: (1) רבי שמעון's measure is one-sixth; (2) cities: return it by the time you could show a money changer; villages: by ערב שבת; (3) a recognized coin must be taken back even after a year; (4) a slightly worn coin is fine for מעשר שני.

phrases.english: And he may give it for second tithe
phrases.notes: He means using the coin to redeem מעשר שני produce, so the holiness moves onto the coin.

phrases.english: and he need not be concerned,
for it is only a miserly soul.
phrases.notes: He means that someone who refuses this coin is just being stingy, not careful about the law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final ruling of the משנה, about the coin's validity for other uses
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slightly worn coin is valid for redeeming מעשר שני; refusing it is only stinginess.

steps.title: The גמרא contrasts the משנה with a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that asks how worn a סלע must be for there TO BE אונאה, the opposite of the משנה's wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They raised a contradiction: how much must a סלע be worn for there to be אונאה in it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by setting up a contradiction. It quotes the opening question of a ברייתא and will compare it to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה asked how worn a סלע can be and still have NO אונאה. The ברייתא lists the same kind of measures but asks how worn it must be for there TO BE אונאה. The same numbers can't mean both 'below this is fine' and 'at this it becomes cheating', so the two sources seem to clash. The answer comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
'And they contrasted it'; introduces a contradiction from another source
A large silver coin worth 4 דינרים
Lacking; worn down
Overcharging or cheating in a sale

phrases.english: Gemara
And they raised a contradiction:
How much must the sela be worn
so that there will be exploitation in it?
phrases.notes: Compare the משנה's opening, which said 'and there will NOT be אונאה in it.' That one word is the whole contradiction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first move: it challenges the wording of the משנה's opening question using a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's question 'how worn can a סלע be and NOT have אונאה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא frames the same measures as the point where אונאה BEGINS, while the משנה frames them as the point where there is still NO אונאה. These are opposite readings of the same measure.

steps.title: רב פפא: the two sources count from opposite directions
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the משנה counts upward from small amounts of wear, while the ברייתא counts downward from large amounts, so they do not truly disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: There is no contradiction. Our משנה counts from low to high, and the outside ברייתא counts from high to low.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from step 5 about why the ברייתא's wording is the opposite of the משנה's. He says both describe the same line, just from different directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה starts from a lightly worn coin and asks how far the wear can go before it becomes אונאה. The ברייתא starts from a heavily worn coin and asks how far down the wear must go before it is no longer אונאה. The cutoff number is the same, so the halacha is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
The תנא of our משנה
The outside תנא, meaning the one of the ברייתא
From low to high

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying the two sources argue about the halacha. The numbers stay the same; only the direction of counting is different.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is not difficult:
The tanna of our mishnah calculates
from low to high,
phrases.notes: He starts from a little wear and works up until it becomes אונאה.

phrases.english: the outside tanna calculates
phrases.notes: The "outside" תנא is the one whose teaching was left out of the משנה, the ברייתא.

phrases.english: from high to low.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 5 between the wording of the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of wording: same cutoff described from opposite directions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's opposite wording suggested it disagreed with the משנה about where אונאה begins.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sources share the same cutoff. One measures upward and the other downward.

steps.title: Why argue about a coin but not about a garment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנאים argue about the measure of wear on a סלע but agree that a טלית uses the measure of one sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a סלע, that they argue, and what is different about a garment, that they do not argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new question for the next steps. Earlier in the פרק everyone agreed that overcharging a sixth on a garment is אונאה, so why do the תנאים argue about coins?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a טלית, the measure of a sixth is accepted by everyone. For a סלע, רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבי שמעון each give a different amount. The גמרא wants to know what makes the coin case open to argument.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
A garment, the standard example of an item sold with אונאה
They disagree

phrases.english: What is different about a sela, that they disagree,
and what is different about a garment, that they do not disagree?
phrases.notes: This refers to the earlier משנה in the פרק where a sixth is the measure of אונאה for anything sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the wording question, the גמרא returns to the משנה's dispute and compares it to the garment rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why there is a dispute about the measure for a worn סלע when there is agreement on a sixth for a טלית.

steps.title: רבא: the garment rule follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the anonymous ruling of a sixth for a טלית is really the opinion of רבי שמעון, who also uses a sixth for a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who taught the law of the garment? It is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the first answer. He says there really is a dispute about garments too, and the garment ruling simply follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is 4 דינרים, and a דינר is 12 פונדיונות. So רבי שמעון's two פונדיונות per דינר equals a sixth, which matches the garment rule. According to רבא, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה would use their smaller amounts for garments too.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught this teaching?
One sixth, the standard measure of אונאה

phrases.english: Rava said: Who taught the case of the garment?
It is Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: His two פונדיונות per דינר works out to exactly a sixth, the same as the garment rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by attributing the garment rule to one side of the dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no real difference. The garment ruling of a sixth matches only רבי שמעון's opinion.

steps.title: אביי: people forgive more on clothing than on coins
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the cases really are different: people forgive up to a sixth when buying clothing, but not on a worn coin that cannot be spent.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: With a garment, a person forgives up to a sixth, as people say, "Overpay for your back, and pay the exact price for your stomach." A סלע, since he cannot spend it, he does not forgive.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer to the question of step 7. He explains why everyone could agree about garments and still argue about coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People are happy to pay extra for good clothing, so a gap smaller than a sixth is forgiven. A worn coin is different, because the person stuck with it cannot pass it on. That is why even a smaller amount of wear may count as אונאה, and the תנאים can argue about how small.

keyTerms.meaning: Forgives, gives up his claim
Overpay for your back, meaning spend extra on clothing
And pay the fair price for your stomach, meaning food
It does not circulate; it cannot be spent

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the garment rule of a sixth follows רבי שמעון only. אביי: everyone agrees on a sixth for garments, because people forgive on clothing but not on a coin they cannot spend.

phrases.english: Abaye said: A garment:
up to a sixth, a person forgives.
As people say:
Overpay for your back, and pay the fair price for your stomach.
phrases.notes: Your "back" means clothing and your "stomach" means food. Spending extra on clothes is worth it.

phrases.english: A sela, since it does not circulate for him,
he does not forgive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: טַלִּית עַד שְׁתוּת מָחֵיל אִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רבא's to the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cases differ. A buyer forgives up to a sixth on a garment, but not on a coin he cannot spend.

steps.title: The full ברייתא: three opinions on a worn סלע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the complete ברייתא: רבי מאיר says one איסר per דינר, רבי יהודה says one פונדיון per דינר, and רבי שמעון says two פונדיונות per דינר. Beyond that, the coin is sold for its worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: How much must a סלע be worn down for there to be אונאה? רבי מאיר says: four איסרות, an איסר per דינר. רבי יהודה says: four פונדיונות, a פונדיון per דינר. רבי שמעון says: eight פונדיונות, two פונדיונות per דינר. If it is worn more than that, he sells it for what it is worth.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא it quoted briefly in step 5 and now brings it in full. This is a new restatement, not a repeat, because it adds the full list of opinions and the final rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A דינר is 24 איסרות or 12 פונדיונות, so the three opinions are 1/24, 1/12, and 1/6 of the coin. The ברייתא also adds a new rule not stated before: once the coin is worn past these amounts, it is no longer treated as a normal coin. It may only be sold for the value of its metal.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; the גמרא returns to quote a source in full
Worn down, missing some of its weight
A small coin, 1/24 of a דינר
A coin worth two איסרות, 1/12 of a דינר
He sells it for its actual worth

steps.whyThisMatters: These numbers explain רבא's answer: only רבי שמעון's measure equals a sixth, which is why he matches the garment rule.

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא: עַד כַּמָּה תְּהֵא הַסֶּלַע חֲסֵירָה
phrases.english: The matter itself: How much must the sela be worn down
for there to be exploitation with it?
Rabbi Meir says: Four issars,
an issar per dinar.
Rabbi Yehuda says: Four pundeyons,
a pundeyon per dinar.
Rabbi Shimon says: Eight pundeyons,
two pundeyons per dinar.
More than that, he sells it for its worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא: עַד כַּמָּה תְּהֵא הַסֶּלַע חֲסֵירָה וִיהֵא בָּהּ אוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא first cited in step 5 and quotes it in full.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: 1/24; רבי יהודה: 1/12; רבי שמעון: 1/6 of the סלע is the measure of אונאה. Beyond that, the coin is sold for its actual value.

steps.title: The ברייתא's limit for a worn coin and what to do with it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a worn סלע may be kept as a coin until it drops to a שקל, and a דינר until a רובע. A coin worn even further may not be spent or sold to people who would cheat with it. It should be pierced and hung on a child's neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much can the coin wear down and one may still keep using it? A סלע, until it is worth a שקל. A דינר, until it is worth a רובע. If it is an איסר less than that, it is forbidden to spend it. He may not sell it to a merchant, a violent man, or a murderer, because they will cheat others with it. Instead he should make a hole in it and hang it on his son's or daughter's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא from the last step. Now it gives the lowest point a worn coin can reach and still be used, and says what to do with a coin that is worn past that point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 dealt with how much wear makes a sale of the coin at full value a cheat. This part sets a second, lower limit: the point where the coin cannot be used as money at all. Past that point the owner must take it out of circulation completely, so nobody can trick others with it.

keyTerms.meaning: wears down, loses value
to keep it (as a usable coin)
a coin worth half a סלע (two דינרים)
a coin called 'rova', explained below as a quarter of a שקל
they cheat, deceive
he should make a hole in it

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different limit from step 10. Step 10 asked when selling the coin at full value counts as cheating. Here the question is when the coin stops being usable money at all.

phrases.english: Up to how much can it wear down
and he still be allowed to keep it (as a coin)?
With a סלע – until it is worth a שקל.
With a דינר – until it is worth a רובע.
If it is an איסר less than that – it is forbidden to spend it.
He may not sell it

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לַתַּגָּר וְלֹא לְחָרָם וְלֹא לְהָרָג,
phrases.english: not to a merchant, not to a violent man, and not to a murderer,
because they cheat others with it.
Rather, he should make a hole in it

phrases.aramaic: וְיִתְלֶנָּה בְּצַוַּאר בְּנוֹ אוֹ בְּצַוַּאר בִּתּוֹ.
phrases.english: and hang it on the neck of his son or the neck of his daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כַּמָּה תִּיפָּחֵת וִיהֵא רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא begun in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סלע may be used until it wears down to a שקל, and a דינר until a רובע. A coin worn further may not be spent or sold to people who might cheat with it. It should be pierced and worn as an ornament.

steps.title: Why does a סלע get half but a דינר only a quarter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out an apparent inconsistency: a סלע may wear down to half its value (a שקל), but a דינר seems to be allowed to wear down to a quarter of its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: a סלע until a שקל, a דינר until a רובע. Why is a סלע different, that it goes until a שקל, and why is a דינר different, that it goes until a רובע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line it just read and asks why the two coins seem to get different limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שקל is half a סלע, so a סלע can lose up to half its value. If 'רובע' means a quarter of a דינר, then a דינר could lose three quarters of its value. There seems to be no reason for such a difference.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the Master said', used to quote back a line from a source just read
what is different? why the difference?

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּסֶלַע עַד שֶׁקֶל, בְּדִינָר עַד רוֹבַע.
phrases.english: With a סלע, until a שקל; with a דינר, until a רובע.
Why is a סלע different, that it goes until a שקל,
and why is a דינר different, that it goes until a רובע?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא בְּסֶלַע עַד שֶׁקֶל, וּמַאי שְׁנָא בְּדִינָר עַד רוֹבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges an apparent inconsistency inside the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's two limits: a שקל for a סלע and a רובע for a דינר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שקל is half a סלע, but a רובע seems to be a quarter of a דינר, so the two coins are given different limits for no clear reason.

steps.title: אביי: 'רובע' means a quarter of a שקל
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'רובע' in the ברייתא is a quarter of a שקל, which equals half a דינר. So the דינר also gets half, just like the סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: what is the 'רובע' that the ברייתא teaches? It also means a quarter of a שקל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by explaining what the word 'רובע' really refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שקל equals two דינרים, so a quarter of a שקל is half a דינר. With that reading, both coins may wear down to half their value, and the inconsistency goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: a quarter of a שקל, which is half a דינר
that (the ברייתא) teaches

phrases.english: אביי said:
What is the 'רובע' that it teaches?
It, too, means a quarter of a שקל.
phrases.notes: 'Too' means it is measured by the שקל, just like the סלע's limit. A quarter of a שקל is half a דינר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inconsistency raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'רובע' means a quarter of a דינר, so the דינר is treated more leniently than the סלע.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'רובע' is a quarter of a שקל, which is half a דינר, so both coins get the same limit of half.

steps.title: רבא supports אביי from the exact word 'רובע'
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the wording of the ברייתא backs up אביי: it says 'רובע', the name of a coin, and not 'רביע', which would simply mean a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the wording is also exact, because it teaches 'רובע' and does not teach 'רביע'. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a proof from the ברייתא's wording that אביי's reading is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא meant 'a quarter of a דינר', it would have used 'רביע', the plain word for a quarter. Choosing 'רובע', the name of a known coin worth a quarter of a שקל, shows it means that coin. 'שמע מינה' closes the point as proven.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also precise (and supports this)
a quarter, a plain fraction
learn from this, it is proven

phrases.english: רבא said: the wording is also exact (in this way),
because it teaches 'רובע',
phrases.notes: רובע is the name of a specific coin, worth a quarter of a שקל.

phrases.english: and it does not teach 'רביע'.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָא תָּנֵי ״רוֹבַע״, וְלָא קָתָנֵי ״רְבִיעַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that 'רובע' means a quarter of a שקל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's choice of the coin name 'רובע' instead of the plain fraction 'רביע'.
steps.whatToRemember: Both a סלע and a דינר may keep being used until they wear down to half their value. The 'רובע' in the ברייתא is a quarter of a שקל, which is half a דינר.

steps.title: Why measure the דינר by the שקל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא describes the דינר's limit as a quarter of a שקל, instead of just saying half a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it need to hang the דינר on the שקל?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know 'רובע' means a quarter of a שקל, the גמרא asks why the ברייתא chose this roundabout way of saying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'half a דינר' would have been simpler and clearer. Measuring a דינר by a different coin suggests the ברייתא wants to teach something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: why does he need to?
to hang it, to make it depend on

phrases.english: Why does it need to make the דינר depend on the שקל?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion of steps 13-14 and asks about the ברייתא's choice of wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא gave the דינר's limit as a quarter of a שקל instead of half a דינר.

steps.title: A side lesson: a worn שקל can become a דינר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא used this wording to teach in passing that a דינר can come from a שקל, meaning a שקל that wore down to half its value is now used as a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us something in passing: that there is such a thing as a דינר that comes from a שקל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the roundabout wording hides an extra lesson about coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שקל worth two דינרים that wears down to half its value is worth one דינר and can be used as one. By tying the דינר to the שקל, the ברייתא hints at this case.

keyTerms.meaning: in passing, along the way
it teaches us
that comes from a שקל

phrases.aramaic: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: It teaches us something in passing,
that there is a דינר that comes from a שקל.
phrases.notes: For example, a שקל that wore down to half its value is now worth just one דינר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording teaches in passing that a worn שקל can end up serving as a דינר.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא measured the דינר by the שקל on purpose, to hint that a שקל worn down to half its value can serve as a דינר.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's lesson, that a דינר can come from a שקל, supports רבי אמי. He rules that a דינר made from a worn שקל may be kept, but a דינר made from a worn סלע may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי אמי. רבי אמי said: a דינר that came from a שקל may be kept and used. A דינר that came from a סלע may not be kept.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the lesson it just drew from the ברייתא matches a ruling of רבי אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worn שקל that is now worth a דינר may be used as a דינר. A worn סלע that dropped all the way to a דינר's value is forbidden, because it is still the size of a סלע and people could mistake it for a full סלע. The ברייתא, by mentioning only a דינר that comes from a שקל, fits this split.

keyTerms.meaning: This supports him
To keep it in use
A דינר that came from a worn-down שקל

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the size and look of a coin matter, and not only its value. A coin must not fool people into thinking it is worth more.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Ami.
For Rabbi Ami said:
A dinar that came from a shekel – it is permitted to keep it.
A dinar that came from a sela – it is forbidden to keep it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the lesson from step 16 to an אמורא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's ruling that a דינר from a שקל may be kept but a דינר from a סלע may not
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's wording, which describes a דינר as coming from a שקל

steps.title: What does 'an איסר less than that' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: 'An איסר less than that – it is forbidden to spend it.' What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא and asks what it means. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'an איסר less than that' is unclear. It does not say less than what, or how the איסר is being measured.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin, worth 1/24 of a דינר
To spend it
What is it saying?

phrases.english: An issar less than that – it is forbidden to spend it.
What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the phrase 'an איסר less than that' means

steps.title: אביי: an איסר more than the measure of אונאה
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a סלע which wore down by an איסר more than the measure of אונאה is forbidden to spend.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this is what it means. If a סלע wore down by an איסר more than the measure of אונאה, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his reading of the unclear line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the ברייתא is measuring from the limit of אונאה, the amount of overcharging people normally forgive. Once the coin has lost an איסר more than that limit, it may not be spent at its full value.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
Overcharging, unfair pricing
It wore down, lost value

phrases.english: Abaye said: this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: פָּחֲתָה סֶלַע יוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי אוֹנָאָה אִיסָּר
phrases.english: If a sela wore down by an issar more than the measure of overcharging
– it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The coin is forbidden once it has lost an איסר beyond the measure of אונאה

steps.title: רבא: then even a tiny amount should be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: if the limit of אונאה matters, then going even a tiny bit past it should already be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: if so, then even the smallest amount should also be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a coin has lost more than the measure of אונאה, any extra loss at all is already real overcharging. So why would the ברייתא wait for a whole extra איסר?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
A tiny amount, anything at all

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If so – even a tiny amount as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading: an איסר beyond the measure of אונאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Anything past the measure of אונאה is already forbidden, so the extra איסר makes no sense.

steps.title: רבא: an איסר per דינר, following רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that a סלע which lost an איסר for each דינר is forbidden, and that this unnamed ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: if a סלע lost an איסר per דינר, it is forbidden. This unnamed teaching follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops אביי's reading and gives his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'איסר' is the measure of loss itself: one איסר for every דינר of the coin's value. That matches רבי מאיר's measure of אונאה, so this unnamed ברייתא follows his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
One איסר for each דינר
An unnamed teaching

steps.whatToRemember: The limit for spending a worn סלע is a loss of one איסר per דינר. The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
If a sela wore down by an issar per dinar – it is forbidden,
and this unattributed teaching follows Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: In the משנה, רבי מאיר set the measure of אונאה at one איסר per דינר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's answer after the challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A loss of one איסר per דינר makes the coin forbidden, following רבי מאיר

steps.title: The משנה in כלים about a worn סלע
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that an invalid סלע set aside as a weight can become טמא. It also teaches that a worn סלע may be kept if it lost up to two דינרים, and must be cut up if it lost more.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: a סלע that became invalid, and someone set it up to weigh with, can become טמא. How much can it wear down and still be kept? Two דינרים. Less than that, he must cut it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a משנה, that sets the limit for keeping a worn סלע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the coin is used as a weight, it counts as a כלי and can become טמא. A coin that has lost up to two דינרים, half its value, may be kept. Past that point, it must be cut so no one passes it off as a real coin.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
That became invalid
Can become ritually impure
He must cut it up

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: The משנה is in מסכת כלים, 12:7.

phrases.english: A sela that became invalid
and he set it up so that he would weigh weights with it
– it can become impure.
Up to how much can it wear down
and he will be allowed to keep it?
(For a sela) two dinars,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. Two דינרים is half a סלע.

phrases.english: less than that – he must cut it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about worn coins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A worn סלע may be kept up to the limit of two דינרים; beyond it, it must be cut up

steps.title: What about the other side of the limit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is for 'more than that.'
steps.simpleTranslation: More than that, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה only gave the rule for 'less than that,' so the גמרא asks about 'more than that.' This sets up the dispute that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording leaves the other side of the two-דינרים measure unexplained. The גמרא wants that case clarified.

keyTerms.meaning: More than that

phrases.english: More than that – what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the case the משנה left out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law for a coin on the 'more than that' side of the two-דינרים measure

steps.title: רב הונא: cut it either way
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the coin must be cut up both when it is less than that and when it is more than that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: less than that, he must cut it; more than that, he must cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the 'more than that' case is treated just like the 'less than that' case. In both, the coin must be cut up.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the strict ruling here

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Less than that – he must cut it,
more than that – he must cut it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In both cases the coin must be cut up

steps.title: רבי אמי: more than that, keep it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי agrees that 'less than that' must be cut up, but rules that 'more than that' may be kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: less than that, he must cut it; more than that, he may keep it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי disagrees with רב הונא on the 'more than that' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree about 'less than that.' They split only on 'more than that': רבי אמי allows the coin to be kept, because no one will confuse it with a real סלע.

keyTerms.meaning: He may keep it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אמי and רב הונא agree on 'less than that.' Their argument is only about 'more than that.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Less than that – he must cut it,
more than that – he may keep it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא on the 'more than that' case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Less than that must be cut up; more than that may be kept

steps.title: The גמרא opens an objection from a teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that it will challenge the rulings just stated, using a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It is about to quote a ברייתא that seems to clash with one of the rulings just given about a worn סלע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיתיבי tells us that a source will be brought to attack something just said. Here, that means the disagreement between רב הונא and רבי אמי about a coin that lost more than two דינרים. The actual challenge is in the quote that follows, not in this word.

keyTerms.meaning: They raise an objection: it introduces a source that challenges what was just said
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה itself
A challenge or difficulty against a statement

steps.confusionAlert: מיתיבי is only the opening. Do not look for the argument here; the objection comes in the quote right after it.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a challenge from a ברייתא against the competing rulings of רב הונא and רבי אמי about the worn סלע.
steps.kashyaTarget: One of the rulings about a סלע that lost more than two דינרים (רב הונא or רבי אמי)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא will be quoted whose ruling appears to contradict one of the two positions; the details come in the next step.
